The Assistant Commissioner of Police, Yeshwanthapura Sub-Division, Bangalore, has submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 to 3 for the offences punishable U/s.498A and 304B r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec.3 and 4 of DP Act in Crime No.193/2019 of Bagalagunte P.S., Bangalore 2.

The factual matrix of the case is that:
The marriage between the daughter of informant by name Smt. Suntha and accused No.1 was solemnized on 27.11.2013 as per the rites and customs prevails in their community.

At the time of marriage the accused persons demanded for one gold ring,
one gold chain and motorbike as dowry, CW.1 and CW.2 have given gold ring and gold chain to the accused No.1 as dowry and unable to give the motorbike as demanded by the accused persons.

After the marriage the the daughter of informant started residing along with accused persons at House SC No.788/2020 bearing No.123, 2nd Floor, 2nd Cross, MTS Colony, T. Dasarahalli, within the limits of Bagalagunte P.S., Bangalore.

Out of the wedlock the accused No.1 and deceased-Smt.
Sunitha blessed with two children.
The accused No.1 doing the buisness of mobile phone sales and service at T. Dasarahalli, Bangalore.

Thereafter the accused No.1 demanded the deceased-Sunitha to bring Rs.5,00,000/- from her parents for construction of house in their site, as at the time of marriage the parents of deceased-Smt. Sunitha have not given any dowry, and used to quarrel with the deceased, the accused No.2 and 3 have also supported for the same.
Thereafter the accused No.1 to 3 subjected deceased to physical and mental cruelty in demanding additional dowry.

Due to unbearable torture of accused persons both physically and mentally the deceased- Smt. Sunitha committed suicide on 4.6.2019 within 4.30 p.m.
at her matrimonial home.

Accordingly, the case was registered against the accused persons for subjecting the deceased for mental and physical cruelty and abetting the deceased to commit suicide in demand of additional dowry within seven years from the date of marriage.

3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the jurisdictional XLV Addl., CMM.,
Bangalore.

The learned Magistrate after taking the cognizance for the offences punishable U/s.498A and 304B r/w Sec.34 of IPC and U/s.3 and 4 of DP Act committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C., furnishing charge sheet copies to the accused persons.

Visited the place of occurrence drawn Ex.P2 mahazar in the presence of mahazar witnesses and PW.15 Raviprasad.P, ACP, Yeshwanthapura Sub-Division, Bangalore, conducted further investigation, filed charge sheet against the accused persons for the alleged offences.
Ex.P16 inquest mahazar and Ex.P17 PM report are marked with consent of bothsides.
It is clear from Ex.P17 PM report that the death of Smt. Sunitha is due to asphyxia as a result of hanging.
The parents, brother, sister and blood relatives of the deceased not supported the case of the prosecution.
There is no evidence to establish the alleged offences committed by the accused herein.
None of the prosecution witnesses supported the case of the prosecution.
Ex.P12 Inquest Mahazar and Ex.P13 Postmortem Report are marked with consent of both sides.
It is clear from Ex.P13 PM report that the death of deceased was due to hanging.

Alleged physical and mental harassment meted out by the deceased after her marriage, giving and taking dowry, at the time of marriage, demand for additional dowry after marriage has not been substantiated by the prosecution.
Prosecution failed to establish that the death of deceased-Mukambi @ Reshma is due to dowry harassment.
17.In 1999 Supreme (Guj) 343 (Indrasing M Rao Vs., State) Hon'ble Gujarat High Court held that The meaning of cruelty is given vide explanation to Sec..498A.
It means willful conduct of such nature, as SC No.788/2020 is likely propel, or goad or compel the women to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb of health.

If the women is subjected to harassment with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand, for property or valuable security or coercing and her relative owing to failure on her or her relatives part to meet such demand, the same would also amount to cruelty.
The expression cruelty means and implies harsh and harmful conduct of certain intensity and persistence.

It, therefore covers the acts causing both physical and mental agony and torture, or tyranny and harm as well as unending accusations and recrimination reflecting bitterness putting the victim thereof to intense miseries and owes strong stirring up her feeling that life is now not worth living and she should die, being the only option left.
The provision of Sec.498A therefore envisages intention to drag or force the women to commit suicide by unabetted, persistent and grave cruelty.

The meaning of word harass which can be found from the dictionary is to subject some one to unbearable, continuous or repeated or persistent unprovoked vexatious attacks, questions, demands or persecutions or brutality, or tyranny or harm or pain or afflictions, or other unpleasantness, or grave annoyances or troubles.
In short what can be said is that Sec.498A will not come in to play in every case of harassment and/ or cruelty.
Reasonable nexus between cruelty and suicide must be established.

It should therefore be Bagalagunte P S vs A1-Ranganath on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129364060/
6 shown that the incessant harassment or cruelty was with a view to force the wife to end her life or fulfill illegal demands of her husband or in laws, and was not SC No.788/2020 matrimonial cruelty namely usual wear and tear of matrimonial life.
It should be hardly stated that the prosecution has to establish the charge beyond reasonable doubt.

No doubt arithmetical accuracy is not expected from the prosecution, but it has to adduce such evidence which would be credible leaving no room to any reasonable doubt"and pointing to the guilt of the accused".
In the case on hand the mother, brother and sister of the deceased examined on behalf of the prosecution deposed that there was no matrimonial dispute between the deceased and accused.
There is no evidence on record to establish that the accused persons received dowry from the parents of the deceased .

In order to hold an accused guilt of an offence U/s.304B of IPC it has to be shown that apart from the fact that the women died on account of burn or bodily injury, otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, it has also to be shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband, or in connection with any demand for dowry.

Only then would such death be called dowry death and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused death of women concerned as held in 2010 AIR SCW 3673(Durgaprasad and another Vs., State of AP).

sentences.text: Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in 2020(5) KCCR 905 (Mahalingappla Vs., State of Karnataka) held that death of victim within seven years from the date of marriage alone can not be ground to convict the accused.

Physical and mental harassment meted out by the deceased resulted in her suicide and receiving of dowry at the time of marriage, demand for additional dowry after marriage has not been established by the prosecution with available evidence on record.
The prosecution has failed to establish the charge leveled against the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, I answer points No.1 to 4 in the Negative.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Alleged physical and mental harassment meted out by the deceased after her marriage, giving and taking dowry, at the time of marriage, demand for additional dowry after marriage has not been substantiated by the prosecution.
Prosecution failed to establish that the death of deceased-Mukambi @ Reshma is due to dowry harassment.
The expression cruelty means and implies harsh and harmful conduct of certain intensity and persistence.
It, therefore covers the acts causing both physical and mental agony and torture, or tyranny and harm as well as unending accusations and recrimination reflecting bitterness putting the victim thereof to intense miseries and owes strong stirring up her feeling that life is now not worth living and she should die, being the only option left.
The provision of Sec.498A therefore envisages intention to drag or force the women to commit suicide by unabetted, persistent and grave cruelty.
The meaning of word harass which can be found from the dictionary is to subject some one to unbearable, continuous or repeated or persistent unprovoked vexatious attacks, questions, demands or persecutions or brutality, or tyranny or harm or pain or afflictions, or other unpleasantness, or grave annoyances or troubles.
There is no evidence on record to establish that the accused persons received dowry from the parents of the deceased .
18.The basic ingredients to attract the provisions of Sec.304B are (i) the death of the women should be caused by burns or fatal injury or otherwise than under normal circumstances;
(ii) Such death should have occurred within seven years of her marriage (iii) she must have been subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband;
(iv)such cruelty and harassment should be for in connection with demand for dowry.
If Sec.304B of IPC r/w Sec.113B of Evidence Act, a comprehensive picture emerges that if a married women dies in an unnatural circumstances at her matrimonial home within seven years from her marriage and there are allegations of cruelty or harassment upon such married women for or in SC No.788/2020 connection with demand of dowry by the husband or relatives of the husband, the case would squarely come under dowry death and there shall be presumption against the husband and the relatives.
In order to hold an accused guilt of an offence U/s.304B of IPC it has to be shown that apart from the fact that the women died on account of burn or bodily injury, otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, it has also to be shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband, or in connection with any demand for dowry.
Only then would such death be called dowry death and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused death of women concerned as held in 2010 AIR SCW 3673(Durgaprasad and another Vs., State of AP).
opennyai_summary.decision:
In view of answer of court on points No.1 to 4, this court pass the following:-
ORDER Acting U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 to 3 are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.498A and 304B r/w Sec.34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3 and 4 of DP Act.
Judgment pronounced in the open court vide its separate order ORDER Acting U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 to 3 are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.498A and 304B r/w Sec.34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3 and 4 of DP Act.
